runs.name: Vistra Corp.; NYSE VST, SEC CIK 0001692819, formerly Vistra Energy Corp.; an integrated retail electricity and power generation company from California to Maine, five reportable segments Retail, Texas, East, West and Asset Closure; Lotus Infrastructure Partners plants bought 2025-10-22; Cogentrix (Q-Generation) signed 2025-12-31, not closed; the 10-K names no rival company, NRG, Constellation and Talen chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief, from scratch. The brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25; the lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the FY2025 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7. Price **$141.73** (close 2026-10-26, aggregator, flagged) x **335,635,195 shares** (10-Q cover for the period ended 2026-06-30, accession 0001692819-26-000019; cover_shares.py) = cap **$47,570M**; sovereign **5.31%** (Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-26). **Q1 IN** (an integrated retailer of electricity, about 5M customers, and a merchant generator of 43,641 MW, 62% gas, 20% coal, 15% nuclear, paid the price the last MWh sets; the ten-year doubt carried to Q2 and Q7). **Q2 IN on the deciding part, Retail** (79% of five-year segment profit as filed, 52% with the hedge marks taken out; Texas customers 2.4M to 2.6M, a profit every year 2021 to 2025 including Winter Storm Uri); generation a price-taker, not the low-cost producer, carried to Q7 at no growth. Peers, the 10-K naming only categories, NRG, Constellation and Talen chosen as a CONVENTION of the run: after-tax operating return on tangible capital Vistra 7.5% (2017-2025), NRG 6.8%, Constellation 7.7%, Talen 1.3% on gapped data, rival figures XBRL transcriptions. **Q3 weighs against** (maintenance and environmental-allowance purchases about $2B to $3B a year). **Q4 weighs against** (Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA featured, guidance given and reaffirmed; the accounts reconcile, no STOP). **Q5 integrity IN** (an Illinois AG complaint and the Ohio HB6 subpoena about conduct before Vistra owned the subsidiaries, an industry antitrust suit; none a finding against present management), ability weighs against narrowly. **Q6 weighs against** (about $6.5B of buybacks funded with debt at roughly $150 a share against the Q7 range, written back). **Q7 OUT, on the floor and above the top of the range**: owner cash all-equity, after all spending, before interest, after a 23% tax (a CONVENTION of the run), the 45U nuclear credit priced separately: -$817M, -$568M, $3,344M, $2,059M, $953M (2021 to 2025); 2021 and 2022 aberrational (Uri, the collateral drain), the base the 2019-2023 cycle as a CONVENTION of the run, $1,562M a year maintenance only; the series changes sign, so the no-growth case alone; purchases of $6,836M exceed half of owner cash, so the organic pair is central and the filer reports no organic growth to credit; preferred stock counted with net debt as a CONVENTION of the run, net debt with preferred $22,549M; Cogentrix signed, FERC-approved, not closed, beside at nothing with its financing and 5,000,000 shares. Value **$26.02 a share all-equity (central)**, literal window beside $17.95 maintenance only and -$5.82 all spending; central yield 2.23% at the price, about 21% a year of growth for ten years needed to earn the floor; **fair price -$15.65 all-equity, not positive**, **$37.80 equity-only**. Facts after the stop recorded, not weighed. Balance sheet: debt about $9.3B (2020) to $19.6B on the face (mid-2026), equity $8.4B to $5.5B of which $2.476B preferred, tangible common equity negative. Strongest evidence against, as the analyst put it: a full cycle of ordinary returns, losses in 2021 and 2022, a price set by other generators, debt-funded buybacks, and a 2023-2025 improvement not yet through a downturn. Framework gaps for the operator: the parts rule on segments that share one fleet and one hedge book (Retail's share an internal transfer price); the fair price of a one-case range; preferred stock in net debt; a production credit booked as revenue under Whose tax; growth spending restated between filings under (e); the named-rival rule when the 10-K names none. Could not get: Retail's own capital, a retail price comparison with rivals, the guidance record across years, cash taxes for 2021 and 2022 (taken as nil). The analyst confessed write-early only partly kept (most research before the Q1 section was written; sections then written and committed in order). Analyst's commits: eight pathspec commits of its own paths, last `6b129f80`. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; 62 id citations resolve, no E-ids, no citation slip, 46 adjacent fragment pairs checked, one checker mispairing resolved by hand (the L2019-006 quote read beside M1998-086; `dispatcher_cite_check2.py`); no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: session-start commit subjects of VGNT, PPL and TAC; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Not armed: the all-equity fair price is not positive and the central figure is already the organic pair; the equity-only $37.80 alert is left to the operator.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7: a Texas-centred electricity retailer with a merchant fleet, Retail deciding at Q2 and the castle standing, but owner cash changes sign across the window and the 2019-2023 cycle yields 2.23% at the price; value $26.02 a share all-equity, the no-growth case alone, against $141.73, debt doubled since 2020 with debt-funded buybacks. Fair -$15.65 all-equity, not positive; $37.80 equity-only; not armed.
